audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave K'Sante four stages and Nautilus none at a 48.93% win rate over 3178 games, and two of those K'Sante rows are contradicted by their own explanations: whys[1] says 'neither of you owns the level outright yet' and whys[6] says 'It stays even'. The packet's chart marks both of those stages Skill.
audit.why: A sub-50 win rate cannot render as a chart K'Sante sweeps, and a row whose prose says 'even' must not display a winner.
audit.corrected: Level 2 and 2+ items flipped to Skill in both layers, proposed as matched pairs. Level 3 and Level 4-5 stay K'Sante — those rows are genuinely his and the prose supports them.

audit.why: Spike order holds: your level-3 combo, your 4-5 control window, level 6 All Out as a double-edged spike, and Nautilus's first-item tank spike where his chain outlasts your cooldowns. Depth Charge and All Out are both 120/100/80, so neither side gets a free ultimate advantage at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three mechanical errors. (1) 'unstoppable' is claimed for Path Maker in four places; Riot's text says only that K'Sante 'charges up, taking reduced damage'. Unstoppable is not in the kit file, and telling a player his W breaks Depth Charge's knock-up is a claim they will die on. (2) 'Q3 knockup' / 'third-cast knockup-pull' — Ntofo Strikes slows and, at TWO stacks, fires a shockwave that PULLS; it never knocks up. The knock-back and stun are Path Maker (W). (3) Nautilus's passive is described as rooting on every marked auto; Riot's text is 'Nautilus' FIRST Attack against a target ... roots them briefly'.
audit.why: All three are stated as decision rules the player acts on: when to spend W, what your trade actually does, and how often you eat a root.
audit.corrected: Path Maker's charge reduces damage taken; the second Ntofo Strikes stack pulls; Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against you. Real numbers added: Dredge Line 14/13/12/11/10s at 1150 range, Riptide 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, Titan's Wrath 12s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing told you to force out Titan's Wrath before committing.
audit.why: Flagged missing interaction 'shield-absorbs-burst': his 12s W shield absorbs exactly the burst window your commit depends on, and its attacks deal damage over time to you while it holds.
audit.corrected: Written into dosFull[2].d — force the shield out first, then commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late were written in the first person ('I only have Q', 'I W-charge', 'I don't bet on out-scaling him'), breaking the second-person voice used everywhere else on the site.
audit.why: The approved quality bar is the user's second-person voice; a first-person paragraph in the middle of a second-person page reads as a different author.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten in second person, inside the length band, with the mechanical corrections above folded in.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — I only have Q and no engage, and Nautilus has his Dredge Line hook but can't all-in either, so I just farm with Ntofo Strikes cleave and don't walk into hook range against the wave. The danger is his passive: every auto after he marks me roots me, so I never trade autos toe-to-toe before I have W. At Level 3 it tips my way — I W-charge a committed Naut for the unstoppable damage-resist window, then land my Q3 knockup-pull, and his single-target hook can't trade back with that.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you only have Q and no engage, and Nautilus has Dredge Line but can't all-in either, so farm with Ntofo Strikes and stay out of its 1150 range with the wave between you. Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against you, so never open a toe-to-toe auto trade before W. At Level 3 it tips your way — Path Maker's charge cuts the damage he returns, then your second Q stack pulls him in, and a 14s hook can't trade back with that.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are my lane-control peak. I trade around his Dredge Line — bait the hook, and once it's down I W in, eat his passive root proc through W's damage resistance, and Q3 him for a clean trade he can't answer. Bank those small leads. At 6 it goes even: All Out gives me a duelist profile that wins the raw 1v1, but it strips my tankiness exactly when his Depth Charge knockup chains into his passive root and E-AOE, so I don't ult into a full-CC Nautilus. Bait his R or his hook first, then commit.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your lane-control peak. Trade around Dredge Line — bait the hook, and inside those 14 seconds you W in, eat the passive root through the charge's damage reduction, and land both Q stacks for a trade he can't answer. Bank those leads. At 6 it goes even: All Out wins the raw 1v1 but strips your resists exactly when Depth Charge knocks you up into Riptide's slow, so never ult into a full-CC Nautilus. Bait his R or his hook first, then commit.

edits.before: This stays a coin-flip into the late game and that's honest — it's a tank mirror where neither of us deletes the other in a sidelane. His first-item spike is his window: a full hook-into-root-into-Depth Charge chain locks me down longer than my W charge can cover, and once W is spent I have no CC immunity left. My edge is teamfights, where R All Out lets me peel a key carry out of his lockdown and my W eats his engage. I don't bet on out-scaling him — I close on my 3-to-5 trading windows and the first reset, then group, because his point-and-click CC reliability matches my peel late.
edits.after: This stays a coin-flip into the late game and that's honest — a tank mirror where neither side deletes the other in a side lane. His first-item spike is his window: hook into passive root into Depth Charge locks you down for longer than one Path Maker charge covers, and Titan's Wrath shields the burst you answer with, so force that 12s shield out before you commit. Your edge is teamfights, where All Out peels a key carry out of his lockdown. Don't bet on out-scaling him — close on your 3-to-5 trading windows and the first reset, then group.

edits.before: Nautilus wastes Dredge Line (Hook) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Force Titan's Wrath's 12s shield out first — it eats your burst window.

notes: The 'unstoppable Path Maker' claim and the 'Q3 knockup' naming both appear across many other ksante pages outside my slice. Neither is supported by the kit file and both are stated as decision rules — worth a repo-wide sweep. The missing interaction 'dash-denied' (Dredge Line denying your W/E/R) was NOT written to the page: Riot's text for Dredge Line describes a pull, not a dash-denial or grounding effect, and I could not verify the claim from the kits.
